messages:
maya: FYI: noticed a bunch of client sessions that show as "connected" in console but upstream pod was drained ~2m earlier. Users saw no reconnect.

sam: ugh. gateway suppressing CLOSEs again? we added that for storm mitigation.

maya: exactly. proxy config seems to suppress socket close events for short drains to avoid a thundering reconnect. but that means our telemetry never records the termination reason. console counts still show active connections.

leo: can you paste the proxy snippet?

maya: 
```proxy:
  suppress_close: true
  suppress_window_ms: 5000
  audible_close_code: 1001  # when we actually want to tell clients
```

maya: that 5s window causes the gateway to swallow the close and just hold the socket open until it reassigns.

tess: so from console perspective session is live; from backend perspective session was terminated -> mismatch for rollouts + billing.

sam: billing dup risk is real. clients that never got a close might continue streaming to fallback model and get charged?

ops-oncall: saw alerts for spike in token usage correlated to the drain window. looks like ~2k sessions that client-side reconnected later once socket actually closed. duplicate tokens for ~10% of those.

leo: two issues then: UX/visibility in console (show suppressed-close state) and telemetry (tag these suppressed closures so we can attribute).

maya: propose: add a suppressed_close telemetry tag + emit a synthetic event when we suppress. console should display as "connected (suppressed-close)" and surface reason on hover.

tess: also we should consider sending a close with code 1001 + reason when upstream is intentionally drained, even during suppression window. that gives clients a deterministic reconnect.

sam: tradeoff: sending close increases reconnect churn. what if we only send close for controlled drains (deploys/canary) and keep suppression for naughty edge cases (network flaps)?

leo: agreed. plan: make suppression conditional: `suppress_close: on_error_only` vs `on_drain`. controlled drains -> explicit close + reason header; errors -> suppress as today.

maya: implementation notes: need a new header from orchestrator -> `X-Upstream-Drain: controlled` so proxy knows when to close. and telemetry key `close.suppressed=true`.

ops-oncall: +1. also add alert for "suppressed_close_count" spike. that will help detect misconfig.

sam: canary plan: roll proxy change to 5% edge nodes, enable explicit close for deploy drains only. monitor duplicate-billing, reconnection rate, and console counts mismatch metric.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: proxy/suppress-close-mode -> 5% at 2026-03-21T15:12Z.

maya: I'll add the console change to show suppressed tag and the hover reason. assigning to @leo for telemetry + @tess for proxy logic.

leo: will add the `close.suppressed` dimension and a synthetic `suppressed_close_event` to the stream of termination events. ETA EOD.

tess: I'll add the `X-Upstream-Drain` header recognition and the two-mode suppress policy. will include tests for billing/dedup path. ETA tomorrow AM.

ops-oncall: if anything goes wrong during canary ping me immediately. I'll watch token-dup and suppressed_close_count.

sam: thanks. follow up: we should also update postmortem checklist to check for suppressed-close misconfigs in future.

maya: agreed. good first step.
